column1: # registry.tsv — build fingerprint (program-image SHA-1) -> expectation set
# Rows added only at freeze time, as a build decision recorded in STATE.md.
# Every row also has an annotated git tag freeze/<expectation-set> at the
# commit that froze it — the way back to a tree that reproduces it.
# THE MERGED BUILD IS FROZEN AND DELIBERATELY HAS NO ROW HERE (merged-m1,
# 14z-92, maintainer-decided). Do not "fix" this by adding one.
# The dispatch fingerprint covers PROGRAM members only (the blind spot
# instrument whose three tenants draw BLANK tiles, packed against the
# zero-filled overlay — is generated from the same inputs as the shippable
# merged build. Both fingerprint 952fc731…, measured. So a row for the
# merged build registers the blanks instrument too, and the guard that
# keeps that instrument out of run_suite IS the absence of this row
# refuses it)"; HANDOFF "never playtest it, never give it a registry row").
# merged-m1 is frozen by annotated git tag + the HANDOFF build-registry row
# instead, and is validated by the merged-specific gates
# audit_select_bank_gates, audit_merged_legacy) rather than by run_suite
# dispatch. If a merged build ever NEEDS run_suite dispatch, the thing to
# change is the discriminator — make the instrument fingerprint-distinct,
# or dispatch on the whole-set fingerprint (build_fingerprint.py --full) —
# never to add a row that silently green-lights the instrument.
# TWO KEY SPACES SINCE 14z-132 (the forward-only whole-set promotion,
# maintainer-ruled). A row's key is just a sha1 and the resolver matches
# either: the WHOLE-SET key first (build_fingerprint.py --set-key, computed
# over the build's OWN rompath dir), then the PROGRAM key, loudly. NEW rows
# carry the whole-set key; the historical rows below keep their program key
# and are not migrated -- 38 of them have no build dir left to compute one
# from (pruned under the N-2 policy) and are inert anyway, since nothing can
# dispatch on a build that no longer exists. MERGED rows are WHOLE-SET-KEYED
# ONLY, which is what lets the merged build have a row at all without the
# program fallback reaching it from `build/merged1`, the blanks-only legacy
# instrument that shares its program fingerprint (see the block above).
# A TRACK NUMBER COUNTS THAT TRACK'S OWN FREEZES AND CARRIES WHEN THE TRACK
# DOES NOT CHANGE, so the numbers of one freeze's four tracks do NOT agree and
# their offsets DRIFT. Measured: at 14z-113 merged went m9 -> m10 alone (the
# one-zip repackaging) while donovan-m14 / huitzil-m21 / pyron-m15 carried
# untouched, moving the offsets from +5/+12/+6 to +4/+11/+5. An offset drift
# is therefore a SIGNAL that a track carried, never an inconsistency to tidy;
# a freeze is named in prose by its MARK, which since 14z-132 is the merged

column3: PYRON M2 FREEZE (14z-76, maintainer playtest + measured, 2026-08-10). = pyron-m1 plus his EFFECT palette block. Delta is EXACTLY two ops: data_file 0x3faba0 (vs2 0x3AC45C, len 0xDC0, into hole_b) + poke32 0x38c25c -> 0x003faba0, i.e. row 0x11 of the effect-palette pointer table. THE PREMISE THAT DEFERRED THIS FOR TWO SESSIONS IS RETRACTED: 0x38C218 was believed to have only SIXTEEN rows, so a variant id would 'index past it' into an adjacent shared table at 0x38C258. It is ONE 32-ROW table indexed by the full character id — the five id-indexing sites take the raw id byte with no mask or fold; 0x38C258 (and 0x38C1D8) have ZERO references in either ROM view; and both tables' variant halves alias the base half except at rows 0x12 and 0x18, which are Oboro Bishamon and its sibling, variant datasets vsav genuinely ships. So row 0x11 is an ordinary variant alias row that legacy never indexes (tests/audit_id_writers.sh), exactly like the sprite row pyron-m1 already carried. Frozen by tests/test_effect_palette_table.sh (4 negative controls). VISIBILITY was NOT decidable by any automated leg — 0 reads of any character's effect block across two full vanilla fighting replays and a 6000-frame Pyron soak, against a live positive control of 60 reads on his sprite block; it is a rare-event palette whose only trigger is the electrocute/status path, which no replay produces. MAINTAINER PLAYTEST decided it: Pyron's shock aura is RED on pyron19 and YELLOW on pyron20, matching vs2; and DEMITRI (whose block Pyron was borrowing, id 0x11 aliasing row 0x01) is identical across both builds and correct — the legacy check no RAM gate can make, because the palette path never transits work RAM.
